subject: Host API / Console: plain-language data transfer & subprocessor phrasing (EU customers)

Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify hosted API data transfer copy for EU customers

Hi Marcus,

We're in the final stages of our procurement review and need a short, plain-language explanation in the Redwood console that summarizes how data may be transferred outside the EU (for hosted API usage) and where we can find the subprocessor list. The current snippet in the console is a bit legal-y and our privacy team asked for: 

- a 1-2 sentence summary suitable for an admin UI tooltip, and
- a link to the full DPA and an up-to-date subprocessor list (ideally with last-updated timestamp).

Attached is a screenshot of what our admin saw (current-privacy-snippet.png). Can you share a couple of short phrasing options and an ETA for when the console microcopy could be updated? This is blocking our PO sign-off.

Thanks,
Jane

On Tue, Mar 30, 2027 at 8:12 AM Jane Smith <jane.smith@acme.com> wrote:
> We're in the final stages of our procurement review and need a short, plain-language explanation in the Redwood console...

Hi Jane — thanks for the flag. We're able to push small console microcopy changes quickly once legal signs off on the wording. I pulled together three short options below (all intended for tooltip/microcopy, ~25-50 words):

Option A (concise): "Redwood may route and store inference requests in regions outside the EU to provide the hosted API. See our DPA and current subprocessor list for details."

Option B (explicit transfers): "Some hosted API traffic may be processed in non-EU regions. We maintain a Data Processing Addendum and an up-to-date subprocessor list you can view for details and transfer mechanisms."

Option C (privacy-first): "To serve requests quickly, Redwood may process data in regions outside the EU. Our DPA explains protections and our subprocessor list shows who helps provide our service."

I'll loop in Kimberly (legal) and Laura (console product) to pick the final language and confirm links. ETA: if we agree on phrasing today, we can ship the console tooltip update to staging within 48 hours and to production the following week (pending translations). Attached: proposed-snippets.txt (raw).

—Marcus

Thanks Marcus — good options. A few legal constraints and recommended edits for public-facing copy: 

- Avoid implying unlimited transfers; use phrasing like "may" or "could" rather than "will."
- Always link the phrase "Data Processing Addendum (DPA)" to the signed DPA or DPA landing page.
- Provide a clear path to the subprocessor list and include a timestamp on that list ("last updated").
- For EU customers, we should add a short parenthetical note about appropriate transfer mechanisms where relevant (e.g., Standard Contractual Clauses, adequacy, or local laws) rather than detailed legalese.

Suggested consolidated microcopy (<= 40 words):
"Redwood may process and store hosted API requests in regions outside the EU. Our Data Processing Addendum and current subprocessor list (last updated: 2027-03-29) describe protections and transfer mechanisms."

If product wants the slightly shorter variant for tooltips, try: 
"Some hosted API requests may be processed outside the EU. See our DPA and current subprocessor list (last updated 2027-03-29)."

I've attached a DPA snippet (dpa-snippet-v2.txt) and a link file for the subprocessor page (subprocessor-links.txt). We should also ensure the console links open in a new tab and that the subprocessor list is machine-readable for customers who pull it.

Kimberly
